answer.rationale: The threat is specifically price-driven churn in the SMB base, so of the five candidates only promotional_pricing addresses the actual mechanism; onboarding, activation, referral and enterprise-assist are good levers but do not answer a competitor price cut to existing price-sensitive SMB accounts. However, I am deliberately holding this to a small, guarded, time-boxed test rather than a broad discount rollout, for a reason the recovered records make explicit: consolidated memory summaries here systematically drop the unfavorable half of the finding. memory_31 was stored as a 'durable lift in first-week activation' but its recovered source (exp_31) also shows 30-day retention -1% and an explicit non-replication outside SMB. memory_86 survived verification cleanly (exp_86: completion +13%, TTV -2.1 days, retention +3%), which tells me the summaries are not uniformly wrong — they are optimistically compressed, and the compression hides exactly the downstream-value terms that matter for my objective. memory_73 ('strong acquisition and revenue lift') is unverified and is the memory most likely to be hiding those terms, because discounting is precisely the lever whose acquisition numbers look best while its margin, LTV, and renewal-price-anchoring costs land outside the measurement window. Acquisition and revenue lift are not the same as sustainable qualified revenue. So: run a narrow test confined to identified at-risk, price-sensitive SMB accounts, with a defined discount floor, an explicit end date, no automatic renewal at the discounted rate, and instrumentation on margin per account, renewal-rate-at-list-price, and expansion — not just booked revenue. Do not extend to new-logo acquisition or to segments where memory_73 was never tested; exp_31 already demonstrated that SMB findings do not travel. In parallel I would keep shipping the onboarding shortening from memory_86, since that is the one claim verified end-to-end with a positive retention term and it costs nothing against price pressure. Top verification priority when the archive reopens is memory_73's source record, specifically its retention, margin, and post-promotion renewal figures; memory_57 and memory_91 carry the same summarization risk and should follow. I am recording that this decision is made on an unverified claim under a spent verification budget, and it should not be read later as confirmation that promotional pricing works.
